== Biography ==
James Glasgow of the Edinburgh Duffe household probably represents [[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow]], the weaver apprenticed in 1641 and admitted burgess in 1649 (70%). On that identification he was born before 16 June 1641, with [[Glasgow-1156|Robert Glasgow]] the preferred probable father (61%). Both the identity and parentage remain inferred; no mother is selected.<ref name="EdinburghOlderWeaver2026" />

He was married to [[Duffe-18|Isobell Duffe]]. Her name is recorded as "Issobell Duff" or "Issobell Duffe" in the christening records of most of their children.

James and Issobell had the following children, all christened in Edinburgh Parish, Midlothian, Scotland:
* [[Glasgow-3088|Jean Glasgow]], christened 13 April 1677.<ref name="Jean1677">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTPF-7YB : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow in entry for Jean Glasgow, 1677.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-3103|James Glasgow]], christened 16 March 1679.<ref name="James1679">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC9-Q9J : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow in entry for James Glasgow, 1679.</ref> (See Research Notes regarding mother's name on this record).
* [[Glasgow-3368|James Glasgow]], christened 18 April 1680.<ref name="James1680">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC9-8S4 : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow in entry for James Glasgow, 1680.</ref> The christening of a second son with the same name strongly suggests the first James died in infancy.
* [[Glasgow-3284|Mary Glasgow]], christened 23 April 1682.<ref name="Mary1682">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQCM-LLH : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow in entry for Mary Glasgow, 1682.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-3285|Thomas Glasgow]], christened 13 November 1684.<ref name="Thomas1684">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC9-N9X : 11 February 2020), James Glascow in entry for Thomas Glascow, 1684.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-2681|Margaret Glasgow]], christened 20 March 1691.<ref name="Margaret1691">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FM3W-XBN : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow in entry for Margarett Glasgow, 1691.</ref>

The date and place of James's death are unknown, but he was alive as of March 1691.
== Research Notes ==
=== Superseded creation estimate ===

The former reasoning was: The parentage and birth date for James Glasgow are not yet known. Based on the birth of his first known child in 1677, he was likely born by about 1657. It is retained here as the history of an estimate, superseded by the conditional older-adult identification.

=== Current Edinburgh older-weaver identity and ancestry — 21 October 2026 ===

James [[Glasgow-2682]], father of the Edinburgh Duffe household, probably represents the same adult as James [[Glasgow-1150]], the weaver apprenticed on 16 June 1641 and admitted burgess on 20 June 1649: 70% subjective identity confidence. The 1696 James and 1699 youngest-son Thomas apprenticeships name a father James Glasgow, weaver and burgess of Edinburgh. Thomas’s maintained 1684 baptismal identification and the Duffe household’s James children of 1679 and 1680 fit those apprenticeship ages and the youngest-son order. The older craftsman independently has that specific craft and civic status, with an exact master/date cross-reference between his 1641 apprenticeship and 1649 admission. The maintained admission review found one matching admission, although this does not establish uniqueness. His marriages to Bessie Whyte on 6 July 1649 and Agnes Duncan on 11 November 1653, followed by Agnes’s burial as the weaver’s wife on 21 January 1674, permit a later Duffe household beginning in 1677. Successive marriages explain the wife sequence without requiring another same-name weaver and burgess.

Select Robert [[Glasgow-1156]] as James-2682’s probable working father at 61%, conditional on that preferred adult identity and the existing 86% identification of the 1641 apprentice’s named father Robert with the Duddingston account buried in 1647. This replaces only the former local Johnne [[Glasgow-1151]] hypothesis, retained unselected at 26%. The live father was blank in the public check on 21 October 2026: the outstanding WikiTree action is a new probable father addition, not replacement of a live father. The 61% and 70% are subjective assessments of nested propositions, not independent confirmations or statistically calculated probabilities.

The main weaknesses are a very long working life and late fatherhood through 1691, together with the absence of a marriage, prior-wife clause, address, witness or admission-date reference directly joining the Duffe husband to the 1649 burgess. The 1693 same-name weaver master is an inferred identification, not an independently dated identity bridge. Another younger Edinburgh weaver and burgess remains possible. The cancelled 1690 Lindsayland apprenticeship could concern the 1696 son, but its deceased father would conflict with assigning that father to the living 1693 master; resolve this before a merge. Retain both James profiles as accounts of potentially one adult, not two proved sons of Robert. Johnne-1151 remains an unselected younger-family alternative at 26%, alongside the James-3076/James-3077 and Annapill Glessie childhood route, John-1084’s Gordon family, and an unrecorded father. Those alternatives are conditional on the Duffe husband being a distinct younger man, not equally compatible with the preferred pre-1641 adult.

The circa-1655 birth, previously inferred from the first known child in 1677, is a creation estimate rather than an age or birth record. The preferred older-adult identity independently supports birth before 16 June 1641, uncertain and conditional on that identity. Replace the local preferred estimate with that boundary, retaining the old circa-1655 and “by about 1657” reasoning as superseded history. This is a separate vital/identity correction, not a date altered solely to fit Robert’s 1647 burial. No exact birth year is established; retain the broad Midlothian birthplace without claiming a new birthplace record.

No mother is selected for James-2682; do not transfer Deborah Ivey or any wife of Robert from the older profile. Robert’s own 28% Corsoun father hypothesis and the older James’s 86% Robert link are unchanged. The 1696 apprentice’s selected father James-2682 remains 82%, probable mother [[Duffe-18]] remains 72%, and brother comparison remains 79%. The two childhood James accounts stay separate. This is a reassessment of held evidence, with no new source discovery, original inspection, profile merger, live edit or confident upgrade. Connectivity counts still describe retained profile accounts and cannot establish their distinctness.

The most useful test is an Edinburgh marriage, guild, property, witness or prior-wife clause linking the Duffe husband to the 1649 burgess. Check the original 1690 cancelled indenture against the 1693 master before identifying that son or merging either James account; inspect the original Duffe baptisms for residence and witnesses. These are targeted next tests, not prerequisites to representing the preferred probable family.<ref name="EdinburghOlderWeaver2026">[https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso28scotuoft/page/71/mode/2up Grant, Register of Apprentices of Edinburgh (1906), printed p.71: James, father Robert, Wester Duddingston, William Sclaitter, 16 June 1641; printed page re-read]; [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=218 Watson, Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses (1929), printed p.208 (PDF p.218): James the weaver, 20 June 1649, matching Sclaitter and 16 June 1641 apprenticeship]; [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_internments_~_greyfriars_churchyard_1658-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=268 Henry Paton (ed.),Register of interments in Greyfriars,1658–1700(1902),printed pp.196,252; PDF pp.212,268]; [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/edinburgh_apprentices_~_1666_to_1700_~_1929.pdf#page=47 Watson,Register of Edinburgh Apprentices,1666–1700(1929),p.37]; [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/edinburgh_apprentices_~_1666_to_1700_~_1929.pdf#page=47 Watson,Register of Edinburgh Apprentices1666–1700(1929),printed p.37]; [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=277 Henry Paton (ed.), Edinburgh marriages 1595–1700, printed p.267/PDF p.277: Bessie Whyte 6 July 1649; Agnes Duncan 11 November 1653; maintained printed-register review reused]. The cited printed registers, apprenticeship entries and parish index associations were already held and reviewed; no manuscript or new original page was inspected for this reassessment.</ref>

Earlier research below is retained as history. Its Johnne26% selection and unchanged-upstream wording are superseded by this dated review; other family grades are unchanged.


=== Current father-profile assessment, 20 October 2026 ===

Preferred father of the 1696 apothecary apprentice, probable 82%; own Johnne father remains uncertain 26%.

Prefer [[Glasgow-2682|James Glasgow (Glasgow-2682)]], the father account defined by the Edinburgh Duffe household, as the 1696 apothecary apprentice [[Glasgow-4114|James Glasgow (Glasgow-4114)]]’s probable father at 82% subjective confidence. The 1696 James and 1699 Thomas entries name their father as James Glasgow, weaver and burgess. Thomas’s maintained identification with the 13 November 1684 child of James and Isobell Duffe gives an entry age of almost fifteen. The household’s James children of 16 March 1679 and 18 April 1680 fit the 1696 entry at seventeen or sixteen. Thomas is the youngest recorded son in this family, consistent with the 1699 indenture’s youngest-son description; the later recorded child, Margaret in 1691, is a daughter. This household-specific age and sibling order gives a better father-profile fit than selecting the older craftsman solely through the repeated occupational description. The James-1150 account remains compatible as another account of this same adult, not an excluded or necessarily different biological father. The 82% assesses the complete father-profile proposition, including Thomas’s inferred apprentice-to-baptism identity and the inferred common father. These clues are related and are considered together, not multiplied as independent confirmations. Neither apprentice entry names a mother, address, father’s admission date or birth date. Another matching family remains possible. The 1679 mother’s Elizabeth/Isobell attribution is retained with its existing qualification. The 1679 and 1680 James profiles remain separate, and neither is selected as the apprentice or Jean Dobie’s husband. Isobell Duffe is not assigned as James-4114’s mother. The possible cancelled 1690 Lindsayland apprenticeship remains unresolved; its father was deceased, while a same-name Edinburgh master appears in 1693. The 1691 baptism alone does not prove its father alive. James-2682’s speculative Johnne-1151 ancestry at 26%, James-1150’s probable Robert-1156 ancestry at 86%, and all vital fields are unchanged. This is a revised local selection; the live father remains blank, so the pending WikiTree action is a new father addition, not replacement of a live parent. The sibling assessment remains 79%.<ref>[https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/edinburgh_apprentices_~_1666_to_1700_~_1929.pdf#page=47 Watson, Edinburgh Apprentices (1929), printed p.37, PDF p.47: James 1696 and Thomas 1699; printed page inspected 18 October, reused]; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC9-N9X Thomas, 13 November 1684: maintained FamilySearch baptism citation]; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC9-Q9J James, 16 March 1679: retained separate child comparison]; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC9-8S4 James, 18 April 1680: retained separate child comparison]; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FM3W-XBN Margaret, 20 March 1691: later daughter, not a younger son]. Prior inspected printed register and maintained baptism citations; no new original inspection.</ref>

=== Edinburgh apprentice family ===
The older Edinburgh weaver [[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow]] remains a compatible possible identity for this James. His wife [[Duncan-16106|Agnes Duncan]] was buried on 21 January 1674, three years before the Duffe child series begins. Different wives therefore do not establish separate men. The circa-1655 birth assigned to the Duffe husband is estimated from his children and does not exclude an older father. Continuing fatherhood to 1691 would nevertheless be late for the craftsman apprenticed in 1641. No marriage, address or wife clause yet identifies their households.

The 1699 baxter apprentice [[Glasgow-3285|Thomas Glasgow]] is described as the youngest son of James Glasgow, weaver and burgess; his maintained identification with the 1684 child fits an entry age of almost fifteen. The 1696 apothecary apprentice [[Glasgow-4114|James Glasgow]] has the same paternal description. They are probable brothers, 79%, from their combined name, craft, civic status and chronology. Two matching fathers remain possible. The 1696 James might be one of the 1679 or 1680 children, but neither identity nor his mother is established.

The speculative [[Glasgow-1151|Johnne Glasgow]] father hypothesis, assessed at 26%, concerns a distinct younger James. It is conditional on the Duffe husband not being the older craftsman, whose apprenticeship instead names father Robert. Both adult accounts and their recorded families remain separate pending resolution of that identity.<ref name="EdinburghBrothersReview">[https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/edinburgh_apprentices_~_1666_to_1700_~_1929.pdf#page=47 Watson, Edinburgh Apprentices (1929), printed p.37, PDF p.47: James1696 and Thomas1699; printed page visually checked18 October2026]; [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_internments_~_greyfriars_churchyard_1658-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=268 Paton, Greyfriars interments1658–1700 (1902), printed p.252, PDF p.268: Agnes Duncan and James the weaver’s unnamed children; visually checked18 October2026]; [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_internments_~_greyfriars_churchyard_1658-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=212 Paton, same register, printed p.196, PDF p.212: Agnes Duncan, wife of James Glasgow,weaver,21 January1674; cross-index of same burial, not independent corroboration].</ref>


=== Selected uncertain Lothian family —16 October2026 ===

Select Johnne [[Glasgow-1151]] as the uncertain working father of James [[Glasgow-2682]], husband of Isobell Duffe. James’s captured biography already proposes Johnne as a possible father. The Inveresk and Musselburgh index records Johnne on25 November 1632 with father Alexander Glasgow. James and Isobell’s Edinburgh children begin with Jean on13 April 1677. If Johnne was baptised near birth and James’s approximate 1655 birth is close, Johnne would have been about 23 at James’s birth and 44 at the first known grandchild’s baptism. This is an ordinary father/son generation within the wider Lothian setting. Select that already recorded comparison provisionally, at very low confidence. Neither James’s own birth nor Johnne’s adult life is established; this is a parent-generation model, not a source naming James’s father.

James [[Glasgow-3076]], recorded at St Cuthbert’s in 1661 with father James [[Glasgow-3077]] and mother Annapill Glessie, remains an alternative childhood identity explicitly suggested in that child’s profile. If baptised as an infant he would have been about 16 at Jean’s 1677 baptism; that younger parenthood makes it less straightforward than the selected ordinary-generation model, but does not exclude him. An older-child baptism also remains possible. John [[Glasgow-1084]] is another previously proposed father. His Gordon/Berwickshire household and separate James [[Glasgow-3107]] account remain viable comparisons; no missing death or marriage is treated as an exclusion. A different unrecorded father remains possible, and the shortlist is not exhaustive. No source joins Johnne’s 1632 child record to an adult father of James, supplies James’s age, or connects their households by craft, witness, property or inheritance. The preference is weak, based on the existing candidate, chronology and regional fit; the component gain supplies no identity evidence. No mother is selected for James. Johnne’s index names Alexander but no mother; his existing Clerk attachment does not establish a mother for James. Retain separate accounts while testing possible identity with [[Glasgow-1150]]; different wives alone do not exclude remarriage. [[Glasgow-1376]] remains unresolved. The old 1657 event on1376 names James as father of Marione, not as the child. That role error does not supply a birth or parentage for the Duffe husband. The old reference to “James-1168,about1540” also mislabels the Corsankell elder; the selected route instead uses Johnne’s actual recorded father Alexander [[Glasgow-1148]]. The 1679 and 1680 sons called James remain separate child accounts; no infant death or survivor marrying Jean Dobie is newly established. The 1679 mother’s indexed Elizabeth/Isobell Duffe difference remains an existing household-identity qualification. All six children, spouse, dates and previous assessments are preserved.

Both father selections are expressly uncertain local hypotheses using existing material. No new mother, original inspection, live WikiTree edit, identity merge or confidence upgrade is claimed. The fixed cohort and all confidently marked connectivity measurements must remain unchanged. Counts describe retained profile accounts and inherit uncertainty in older links, including possible duplicates. <ref>Existing reviewed indexes: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4V-PQK Johnne,Inveresk 1632], SP 689,10/226; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTPF-7YB Jean,Edinburgh 1677], James/Isobell Duffe household; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-X6G Johne,Kirknewton 1649], father Johne; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-ZQN Bessie,Kirknewton 1682], William/Ann household. These support explicitly uncertain generation/locality selections, not direct parent clauses for the two adults; no original newly inspected.</ref>


'''Identifying the parents of James Glasgow is a top research priority.''' Earlier comparisons included the following James accounts; their wives alone do not rule out sequential marriages:
*   '''[[Glasgow-3098|James Glasgow (b. 1631)]]''', who was married to Bessie Whyte.
*   '''[[Glasgow-3077|James Glasgow (b. bef. 1640)]]''', who was married to Helen Clerk.
*   '''[[Glasgow-3337|James Glasgow (b. ca. 1640)]]''', who was married to Annapill Glessie.

The old Whyte groom account [[Glasgow-3098]] is now represented by [[Glasgow-1150]]. Agnes Duncan’s 1674 burial permits a later Duffe marriage. [[Glasgow-3337]] is represented by [[Glasgow-3077]]; these names must not be counted as four independently proved adults.

*   '''Parentage is Unknown:''' The parents of James are not yet confirmed. The original profile suggested he might descend from the Midlothian line of [[Glasgow-1168|James Glasgow (abt.1540-1580)]], perhaps as a son of [[Glasgow-1151|Johne Glasgow (1632-)]] or [[Glasgow-1084|John Glasgow (bef.1616-)]]. This is speculative and requires further research to find a primary source linking him to a father.
*   '''Conflicting Mother's Name:''' The 1679 christening record for his son [[Glasgow-3103|James]] lists the mother's name as "Elizabeth Duffe" instead of "Issobell". As all other children's records name her as Issobell, and given the commonality of clerical errors, it is most likely that "Elizabeth" was a mistake by the parish clerk.
*   '''Future Research:''' The highest priority is to find a marriage record for James Glasgow and Issobell Duffe in the Edinburgh parish registers, likely dated before April 1677. A search for burial records for both James and Issobell after March 1691 should also be conducted.
